hypothesis: The current ETH and SP500 exit controllers remain mechanically intact, while the reversal of the still-open ETH native-versus-R5 snapshot comparison demonstrates that a selected provisional giveback boundary cannot establish an exit-policy edge.
decision: Keep both open lifecycles under their bound V58 execution plans and make no live exit-policy or order change from this prefix. ETH remains protected, has no ignored opposite exit or persistent structure-opposition trigger, and remains structurally supported. The same predeclared R5/2R challenger that was estimated 3.44 USD ahead at the prior open prefix is now estimated 0.69 USD behind the later exit-now reference on the excluding-funding comparison. This reversal strengthens the requirement to judge the native and rejected challenger paths only after the authoritative close rather than selecting a policy from one favorable open snapshot. SP500 remains protected and still has only 22.14 bps MFE, below both its live 100-bps activation and the lowest 25-bps report-only challenger. Reconcile both authoritative closes before judging economic exit quality.
falsifier: Revise immediately if either owned stop disappears, an eligible opposite intent is not acted on, a close lacks an attributable reduce-only lifecycle, or terminal exact-cost evidence materially changes the native-versus-predeclared challenger comparison. Reopening the rejected ETH R5/2R policy broadly requires genuinely future both-side resolved evidence rather than this single selected long path.
